title: Deciding on music and the musicians around his aunts
summary: He always wanted to play; his aunts' musician friends, including an alto player at Xavier, and aunt Angelina Campbell.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So, was there a certain point in time where you decided you were going to make music your life, you were going to be a professional musician?

Always. From a young man. From a young man. From the day I left that show, seeing a little kid on top of the piano playing the trumpet, I wanted to play music. Because people who visited my house, you see we had a family that lived all together, my aunts, my uncles, my grandmother, my grandfather, my mother, my father, and all these. So they had, and these older aunts, they went to Zav University and they also went to Dillard University. And in those days they had musicians like William Houston, William Houston Junior, not William Houston the Third. Mm-hmm. But William Houston Junior was my aunts' boyfriend. So those musicians that came around all the time, man. Let's see, he played alto saxophone and he went to Zav University. Oh man, I'm trying to think of, he was a very popular alto saxophonist. And I can't think of his name. Oh man. But anyhow, he was my aunts' boyfriend also.
You see? And he came around all the time.
You had a lot of musicians coming in.

Oh yeah. Oh yeah, yeah. And my aunt, one of my aunts played piano. And she taught at school. She was also, she always so became a principal. As a matter of fact, I just found out that she is the first black female, American, to graduate from Columbia University. Wow. Yeah. Her name is Angelina Stevenson Campbell. She was a Jollibee. And she used to be principal of a couple of high schools here. So she's still living. She's 93 years old now. She's. Yeah. And so, I can't think of the alto man's name, you know, like a tab hunter or either a lucky or damn, why can't I think of him?
Local guy? Local, from New Orleans?

Well no. He came to study at Zav. He came to study music and other things. He wasn't, his home wasn't here. But he became very popular. He was a very popular alto saxophonist. Like Coleman, like, who was his name that played with alto? Duke. I'm forgetting all these people's names. Boyhood heroes too.
